scope: Illustrative specifications and interface contracts; not a purchasing list, price survey, installed qualification or guarantee that a named cell meets the current controller assumptions.

sources.title: Mini27 Titanium force/torque sensor
sources.notes: Published stiffness is calculated; quoted effective resolution is interface-dependent and includes dropping noisy counts. Accuracy requires manufacturer information. Sensing range and combined-load envelope are distinct from single-axis overload survival. These are examples of realistic stiffness and capacity, not the ADC resolution of our custom board.

sources.title: Mini40 force/torque sensor
sources.notes: A compact force/torque cell need not share the model's 64 MN/m axial stiffness. Its standalone catalog resonance is not the loaded flange mode.

sources.title: Mini45 force/torque sensor
sources.notes: Stiffness differs from both Mini40 and the selected model, so installed modal identification remains necessary.

sources.title: 3A60A three-axis force load cell current specifications
sources.notes: Three force axes can use three ADC inputs, but axis count alone does not meet accuracy/stiffness targets. Derived stiffness uses rated force divided by rated deflection. Derived mode assumes S constrained by maintained contact and B=0.6 kg; it is an illustrative scale calculation, not a simulated or measured flange resonance. The current page's hysteresis value controls this review.

sourceDisagreement.resolution: Use the current manufacturer page conservatively and obtain the exact quoted-unit datasheet before selection; do not silently use the better historical figure.

sources.title: DAQ force/torque sensor manual, section 3.3 Load Calculation
sources.notes: Six raw strain channels jointly reconstruct a wrench through a calibration matrix. They are not six separately measured Cartesian force axes. Keeping only axial/transverse force outputs does not generally permit dropping raw channels from an integrated six-axis cell.

sources.title: Force/torque system interfaces
sources.notes: Analog raw/TWE sensors require customer amplification and digitization. A digital sensor contains that acquisition internally, so a separate load-cell ADC chip is optional. Those listed digital interfaces have different response/timing from the selected 30 ksample/s synchronized chain and are not drop-in qualified replacements. ATI also states that frequency response depends on mounted tooling mass and configuration.

sources.title: Axia80 and RS485 interface manual
sources.notes: A fast-looking digital packet rate can repeat older ADC values; the manual distinguishes sample rate from data rate. The M20 factory accuracy example shows why fine digital resolution alone cannot guarantee ±0.5 N calibrated force accuracy. This is one product example, not a claim about every digital sensor.

sources.title: Load Cell 301 Guide, revised 2024
sources.notes: Primary-axis stiffness can be estimated from rated force and deflection, whose values are generally typical rather than controlled. Low-cost utility cells may have important off-axis coupling. Loaded response depends on attached mass, and side loads/moments require mechanical isolation or characterized rejection.

sources.title: LSB205 miniature S-beam load cell specification
sources.notes: Illustrative single-axis bridge: 2 mV/V at full load gives only 10 mV at 5 V excitation. It needs amplification and digitization; nominal bit count does not remove hysteresis or missing drag information.
